name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may repeatedly try passwords or credentials against accounts until a valid login is found.
detection_ideas: Look for repeated failed logins from the same source.
Track high failure counts against privileged accounts.
Alert on impossible travel with authentication failures.
mitigation: Enable account lockout or rate limiting.
Block malicious sources and reset impacted credentials.

name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
description: Adversaries may use legitimate user or service accounts to access systems and evade basic detection.
detection_ideas: Monitor privileged account logins from unusual hosts.
Review first-time account usage on sensitive systems.
Correlate successful logins after repeated failures.
mitigation: Review stale accounts and rotate credentials.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command shells and scripting engines such as PowerShell to execute malicious commands.
detection_ideas: Alert on encoded PowerShell commands.
Inspect suspicious parent-child process chains.
Look for script interpreters downloading or executing remote content.
mitigation: Restrict unsigned scripts and suspicious interpreters.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries may inject code into legitimate processes to hide execution or gain privileges.
detection_ideas: Look for CreateRemoteThread or suspicious handle access.
Correlate process injection alerts with unusual child processes.
Monitor unsigned code in trusted processes.
mitigation: Use endpoint protection with behavior blocking.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries may steal data by sending it through command-and-control or other outbound channels.
detection_ideas: Alert on large outbound transfers to uncommon destinations.
Monitor suspicious beaconing followed by upload activity.
Correlate sensitive file access with outbound network spikes.
mitigation: Block suspicious destinations and preserve network evidence.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries may send malicious emails or messages to trick users into opening links, attachments, or entering credentials.
detection_ideas: Detect suspicious attachment names and sender spoofing.
Correlate reported messages with URL clicks.
Search for credential-harvesting language.
mitigation: Train users to report suspicious messages.
Block malicious senders, URLs, and attachments.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries may use remote services such as RDP, SSH, SMB, or WinRM to move across systems.
detection_ideas: Monitor remote logons from unusual hosts.
Track lateral movement after credential alerts.
Alert on remote service access by privileged users.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Adversaries may gather system information to learn hostnames, users, operating systems, and environment details.
detection_ideas: Look for discovery commands run by unusual users.
Correlate discovery commands with later lateral movement.
Detect scripted execution of host inventory commands.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries may transfer tools or payloads into an environment from external systems.
detection_ideas: Detect command-line download utilities.
Look for script download cradles.
Correlate downloads into temporary directories with execution.
mitigation: Inspect downloads and enforce application control.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries may dump credentials from operating system stores such as LSASS or security databases.
detection_ideas: Alert on suspicious LSASS access.
Detect credential dumping tools.
Monitor registry hive exports and memory dumping behavior.
mitigation: Use endpoint controls to block credential dumping tools.
